To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the B -> pi pi decay is sensitive to the Delta I = 1/2 and Delta I = 3/2 amplitude components, while B -> rho rho is sensitive to the amplitude components Delta I = 0, 2 and 4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for a new physics contribution to the B -> VV decays.
the search for the Delta I = 3/2 amplitude component in B -> rho rho decaying through the intermediate states rho pi, rho rho, rho eta, and rho omega.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isospins are not closing, but we are not yet able to say why.
there is no compelling evidence for the presence of the Delta I = 1/2 amplitude in B(Bbar) ---> pi pi decays.
there is no evidence for a Delta I=5/2 component in the B -> pi pi decays, but the situation is not yet clear for B -> rho rho decaying to the rho pi pi final state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current data are not sufficient to determine if the Delta I = 1/2 amplitude is the dominant one in these decays.
the current B -> pi pi data are consistent with the Delta I = 1/2 component alone, while the current B -> rho rho data are not.
we find that the B -> pi pi data is not yet precise enough to rule out the Delta I = 1/2 component, but that the B -> rho rho data does not show the same hint of a Delta I =5/2 component.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, if the Delta I = 1/2 and Delta I = 3/2 amplitudes are known from B -> pi pi, then the B -> rho rho data can be used to constrain the Delta I =5/2 amplitude, even in the presence of a large background.
the Delta I = 3/2 amplitude in B(Bbar) --> rho rho decays is not necessarily a good proxy for the same amplitude in B(Bar) --> pi pi decays.
the Delta I = 1/2 component in B(Bbar) --> rho rho decays is very small, and thus the Delta I =1/2 and 5/2 amplitudes are almost completely decoupled.
